chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who said to another man, 'A thousand dirhams are owed by you to me.' The man said, 'No, but it is an entrustment (deposit).' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The word is the word of the owner of the wealth, along with his oath.'
ai.seo_question: How is a financial dispute resolved when one party claims a debt and the other claims it is a deposit?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'Al-Qawl bi-Qawl Sahib al-Mal' (the word of the owner prevails with an oath), a foundational rule in Shia fiqh for resolving conflicting claims regarding debt versus deposit. It underscores the evidentiary weight of the oath (yamin) in civil disputes, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on procedural justice and the presumption of ownership in the absence of contrary proof.
